title: Elasticity: latency & cost — Violin-style benchmark memo
content:
Purpose:
This note captures exploratory bench runs that compare latency distributions and per-token cost across a small set of elasticity scenarios. The goal is to produce compact, communicable shapes (violin-like textual plots and percentile tables) that help product and SRE decide which autoscale/profile knobs to expose to customers.

Scope and constraints:
- Service: hosted text-generation (causal) route mapped to 8xA100-equivalent pool (mixed GPU flavors emulated).
- Model: open-llama-13b-consistent-8k (same weights, mixed-quant config).
- Workload scenarios: three traffic shapes simulated over 2 hours each: steady (constant 200 RPS), spike (idle -> 1500 RPS for 90s, back to idle), and ramp (0->500 RPS over 120s, sustain 500 for 30m).
- Client request profile: 1–3 prompts/session, mean prompt length 80 tokens, mean generated tokens 120.
- Key knobs evaluated: min-instances (1 vs 4), burst-capacity enabled/disabled, batch size cap (16 vs 64), prewarm window (off / 60s).
- Cost metric: approximate GPU-second amortized per 1k output tokens (includes idle amortization during min-instances). We used internal cost model v2 (see linked artifact).
- Latency metric: p50/p90/p99 of server-to-client first-token and end-to-end completion time.

Methodology notes (short):
- Each scenario repeated 3 times; results averaged with run-to-run std annotated where large.
- KV cache disabled for these runs to isolate elasticity effects (we'll run cache-on later).
- No user-level retries; client concurrency tuned to saturate target RPS.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Elastic deployments with higher min-instances (4 vs 1) consistently reduce p99 first-token latency by ~30–50% under spike and ramp scenarios at the expense of ~18–25% higher baseline cost per 1k tokens. Allowing larger batch caps (64) reduces median token cost in steady workloads by ~12% but increases p90 latency by ~10–15% during spikes. Enabling a short prewarm (60s) with burst-capacity gives the best combined sweet-spot for interactive SLAs: p90 within 120–180ms and cost within +8–12% of the baseline steady minimum-instance configuration.

Representative numeric table (averaged across repeat runs):
Scenario | Config (minInst, batchCap, prewarm) | p50 first-token (ms) | p90 first-token (ms) | p99 first-token (ms) | cost per 1k tokens (GPU-sec)
Steady | (1,16,off) | 48 | 95 | 210 | 0.85
Steady | (4,64,off) | 52 | 115 | 240 | 0.75
Spike | (1,16,off) | 120 | 320 | 980 | 1.20
Spike | (4,16,off) | 70 | 145 | 460 | 1.40
Spike | (4,64,60s) | 60 | 130 | 300 | 1.12
Ramp | (1,16,off) | 90 | 210 | 720 | 1.05
Ramp | (4,64,60s) | 58 | 140 | 330 | 1.10

Notes on the table:
- Cost numbers include amortized idle GPU seconds for min instances. The lower cost in the steady (4,64,off) result is due to higher batching efficiency; note the latency trade-off.
- Spike (1,16,off) shows severe p99 tail; this is what customers experience when we rely on on-demand cold-starts with low min-instance.

Violin-style ASCII summaries (purpose: quick visual cues for slack/PRD snippets). We encode relative density by ASCII width. Each violin represents the p0–p100 density shape of first-token latency; scale is approximate.
Legend: '-' low density, '=' medium, '#' high density, '|' median marker
Steady / (1,16,off):
  0-50ms  : --==###==--
  50-150ms: --==##=-----
  150-400ms: --=--#-------
  400ms+  : --=----------
  median | at 48ms

Spike / (1,16,off):
  0-50ms  : --=----
  50-150ms: --==##==
  150-400ms: --==###==
  400-1000ms: --==##===#
  1000ms+: --=-----
  median | at 120ms

Ramp / (4,64,60s):
  0-50ms  : --==###=--
  50-150ms: --===##==--
  150-350ms: --==#=-----
  350ms+: --=--------
  median | at 58ms

Interpretation of violins:
- Wider clusters around higher latency indicate heavy tailing under autoscale-on-demand behavior.
- Configs with higher min-instances compress the violin toward lower latency but can leave residual medium-latency mass if batch caps increase wait time.

Key tradeoffs and recommended defaults for hosted API (opinionated):
1) Default min-instances=2 for interactive tiers (developer/small prod). Rationale: cuts p99 materially for short spikes while keeping committed cost moderate.
2) Burst-capacity ON for all tiers but with adaptive prewarm: if route receives >X RPS sustained for Y seconds, proactively spin additional instances to the route’s historical peak (X/Y heuristics).
3) Expose batch_cap knob only to power-users with clear warning: larger caps reduce cost at steady rates but may worsen p90/p99 on transient bursts. Default batch_cap=32.
4) Add a "short prewarm" option (30–60s) for routes tagged as low-latency; this should be a paid feature for enterprise.

Observability and UX collateral to ship with defaults:
- Dashboard tile: "Elasticity violin" per route showing recent 1h/24h violin plots for first-token latency.
- Alert: p99 > 500ms and burst requests > 2x baseline should surface a suggestion to increase min-instances.
- Cost explainer: small chart inline showing cost delta vs p99 (two-axis) for chosen knobs.

Open questions / next runs (action items):
- Re-run with KV cache enabled (expected: tails compress heavily; measure interaction with batch caps). Owner: Liam. Target: 2026-01-10.
- Evaluate per-tenant isolation (virtualized GPUs) effect on latency violin shapes. Owner: Marisol. Target: 2026-01-20.
- Sensitivity sweep of prewarm duration (0,15,30,60,120s) for short spikes (30–180s) to find knee point. Owner: Anoop. Target: 2026-01-14.
- Add energy/thermal transient measurement for long ramps—possible correlation with internal throttle events (infrastructure). Owner: SRE rotation.

Appendix A — quick reproducibility notes:
- Run harness: tools/bench/harness-elasticity v0.9
- Config snippet used in runs: routeConcurrency=auto; clientBurstProfile=spike-1500; batchWindowMs=10; batchCap=[16|64]; minInstances=[1|4]; prewarmSec=[0|60];
- Data artifacts: run logs stored on s3://redwood-bench/elasticity/2025-12-15/ (internal access only).

Appendix B — short bullet of conversation-ready points for PM/CS sync:
- "If you want lower p99 for interactive features, raising min-instances is a predictable lever — expect ~20% cost uplift for large p99 improvements during spikes."
- "Batching is our best steady-state cost lever, but it's a double-edged sword for latency under bursty customer traffic."
- "Short prewarm windows are high-payoff and should be productized as a tier option."

If you want, I can turn the ascii violins into small sparklines (png/svg) for the docs branch. For now storing raw bench outputs + this memo.

-- Evelyn
